nodes.name: Get All Posts
nodes.notes: TODO(Alan): create a Sheet named 'Posts' with columns: postText, imageUrl (optional -- see deviation note below), scheduledDate (YYYY-MM-DD), status (pending/posted/failed), postId, postUrl. DEVIATION from the YouTube/Facebook/LinkedIn pattern, flagged not silent: this column is 'imageUrl', not 'imageFileId'. Threads' Content Publishing API only accepts a publicly-reachable image URL for image posts (no binary/multipart upload) -- so a Google Drive file ID doesn't work here directly. Alan must host the image somewhere with a public URL (a public Drive 'anyone with the link' share URL may work but is unverified against Threads' fetcher; a dedicated image host is more reliable) and put that URL directly in the row.

nodes.name: Filter Ready To Post
nodes.notes: Known n8n import quirk (same as YouTube/LinkedIn/Facebook builds): this Filter node's Value fields sometimes need to be re-typed by hand in the UI even when the JSON looks correct.

nodes.name: Create Media Container (Image)
nodes.notes: BLOCKED as of 2026-07-27 -- see docs/threads-scheduled-post-workflow.md 'Blocker' section. n8n has NO dedicated Threads node (confirmed live in the node picker: searching 'Threads' returns 'We didn't make that... yet -- you can probably do it with the HTTP Request node'), so this uses a generic HTTP Request node against Threads' own Graph API host (graph.threads.net, NOT graph.facebook.com -- Threads has a separate API surface from the main Facebook Graph API). Threads' two-step publish flow: (1) this node creates a 'media container' and returns a creation_id, (2) 'Publish Media Container' below actually posts it. Also requires the 'threads_content_publish' permission, which is NOT yet added to Alan's Meta app's Threads API use case (only 'threads_basic' is). Also requires a SEPARATE Threads App ID/Secret (Threads app ID 1047046641402198 was visible in the Meta console 2026-07-27, but its secret was not read/copied) -- distinct from the Facebook App ID/Secret Alan already supplied, which only authenticates the Facebook Graph API side, not Threads. REPLACE_WITH_THREADS_USER_ID is the Threads user/profile ID (obtained via GET /me on graph.threads.net once a Threads credential exists) -- not yet known. Built entirely from Meta's public Threads API documentation, not a live test execution -- sanity-check every field name before running.

nodes.name: Create Media Container (Text)
nodes.notes: Same BLOCKED status and same caveats as Create Media Container (Image) -- see that node's notes and docs/threads-scheduled-post-workflow.md.

nodes.name: Publish Media Container
nodes.notes: Second step of Threads' publish flow -- takes the creation_id (id) returned by whichever 'Create Media Container' node ran, and actually publishes it. Meta's docs recommend a short delay before publishing (they suggest polling the container's status_code until FINISHED, mainly relevant for video); for text/image this is usually near-instant but not guaranteed -- flagging as an unverified assumption, not built here, since it can't be tested against a live credential yet.

nodes.name: Posted OK?
nodes.notes: Assumes threads_publish's response has an 'id' field (the published Thread's ID) on success, per Meta's published docs -- unverified against a live call. Confirm on first real run.

nodes.name: Update Row Status
nodes.notes: Matches by row_number, same pattern as the LinkedIn/Facebook builds. postUrl format ('threads.net/t/{id}') is a best-guess based on Threads' public URL shape, not verified -- confirm once a real post succeeds.

nodes.name: Notify Success (Gmail Draft)

parameters.subject: ={{ 'Threads post succeeded' }}
parameters.message: ={{ 'Post text: ' + $('Filter Ready To Post').item.json.postText + '\nScheduled for: ' + $('Filter Ready To Post').item.json.scheduledDate + '\nURL: https://www.threads.net/t/' + $json.id }}

nodes.notes: Matches the Gmail-draft notification pattern used across every other automation in this repo.

nodes.name: Notify Failure (Gmail Draft)

parameters.subject: ={{ 'Threads post FAILED: ' + ($json.postText || '').substring(0, 60) }}
parameters.message:
={{ 'Post text: ' + $json.postText + '
Scheduled for: ' + $json.scheduledDate + '
Error: ' + JSON.stringify($json.errorBody) + '

Row status was NOT updated, so it will retry next run.' }}

nodes.notes: TODO(Alan): decide if repeated-failure rows should auto-flip to status=failed after N retries instead of notifying forever, same open question as every other workflow in this repo.
